passages.text:
Re: Potential synergies with YouTube
Wednesday, September 21, 2022 at 1:42:58 PM Eastern Daylight
[contact omitted] Joshua Machleder
Time
To: [contact omitted] Tinaflor Chaingam
Cc: [contact omitted] Christopher Adams, [contact omitted] Elizabeth Callender, [contact omitted] Leslie
Maccracken, [contact omitted] Nils Mueller, [contact omitted] Vera Zakem
Hey Folks --
Just picking back up on this discussion. As I mentioned to some of you last night, YouTube (Josh Blumenfeld, Emily
Keller, Meredith Cherwony) is interested in moving ahead on this! Which is great.
I will send later today YouTube's edited response to Internews' concept -- they've narrowed the scope to the areas where
they feel that YouTube's contribution fits best with their strategy, defined the areas where YouTube will contribute in-kind
(through staff time/training, etc.) and, accordingly, the budget (brought down to approximately $170K). I think that despite
Internews' ambitious concept ($1million) this is a pretty good outcome as it is both realistic in terms of what kinds of
contributions we get from the private sector (actually, quite good, when you consider we're leveraging a $500k activity),
and it's a pilot for the kind of cooperation that, if it goes well, we can build upon in the future with YouTube.
Some matters that we talked through today, in brief, included: executing this in a way so that YouTube funding would go
directly to Internews (rather than through USG), issues that Nils and Elizabeth raised in terms of the timeline -- which can
be flexibly adjusted to the USAID funding (as INSPIRES work needs to close by September 2023).
Some next steps :
1) share with RDMA and Internews YouTube's scoped down version of the concept:
2) schedule and take a call with YouTube, RDMA, and Internews next week to discuss the scoped down version of the
concept; and if that goes well,
3) leave YouTube and Internews to negotiate the budget-breakdown and execute a contract. They're quite ready to move
on something quickly (although contracting is never such a rapid process).
I'll be talking to some of you later today (Wednesday evening DC time, Thursday morning Bangkok time), so if there are
any questions/issues, we can sort through those. I'm trying to be mindful of effectively, but also quickly communicating
about this through the "four corners" (USAID/DC, USAID/RDMA, Internews Asia, Internews DC).
l've copied +Vera Zakem here. Vera, please let me know if I left out some key piece of information from the discussions
earlier today with YouTube or didn't adequately convey any details.
Thanks!!!
Best,
Josh
On Fri, Aug 5, 2022 at 9:13 AM Tinaflor Chaingam <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Hi Josh,
Chris and I have no issue sharing Internews' proposes activities with Vera Zakem. Please feel free to share the
attachments with her so she can socialize with YouTube about it.
Thank you,
Tina

Best,
Josh

Hi Nils, Tina, Josh, Elizabeth, Chris, Leslie
Please find attached our proposed activities for the USAID - YouTube collaboration along with a skeleton budget for your
review. If you have any questions or feedback please let me know.
Pleasecouldyoualso letus know what the next step is and what is the process with engaging with YouTube.
We are excited about the potential of this opportunity and look forward to making it happen.
Best Rowan
From: Nils Mueller <[contact omitted]>
Sent: Saturday, 23 July 2022 3:51 AM
To: Rowan Reid < [opaque block] [contact omitted]>
Cc: Tinaflor Chaingam <[contact omitted]>; Brian Hanley < [opaque block] [contact omitted]>; Amy Sim
[opaque block] [contact omitted]>; Dan Spealman < [opaque block] [contact omitted]>; Rafiq Copeland < [opaque block] [contact omitted]>;
Erzabeth Callender <[contact omitted]>; Leslle Maccracken<[contact omitted]: Christopher Adams
<[contact omitted]>; Joshua Machleder <[contact omitted]>
Subject: Re: Potential synergies with YouTube
Hi all, andthank you Rowan for your response.
We agree that there are potential synergies between the YouTube concept and component 2 of the "Media and HR in SE
Asia" activity.
Unfortunately we have a bit of a time crunch on the need to express interest in taking the next step on a potential
partnership with YouTube given internal timelines. Please see the linked draft concept note (please keep it close hold
and do not distribute further) for more information on the concept. You'll note that USAID/YouTube intend to select the
two sub-regions by Sept. 1 (including having draft MOUs in place), and in speaking with Vera Zakem, USAID's new
Senior Advisor on information resilience/disinformation issues, she needs to know by the end of next week if we can take
the next steps, which would involve connecting YouTube with Internews. Vera Zakem is the POC on the USAID side for
the concept.
An important positive aspect of the partnership, as I understand it, is that YouTube would bring their own additional
resources tothe table forthe activity, which would expand our ability to have more impact via the activity. Something that
we would need to consider is how to manage the marketing/branding/PR aspect of the partnership as YouTube will want
to publicize the partnership with USAID.

Myconcern is that if we do not signal our interest in moving forward with direct engagement with YouTube by the end of
next week, we will miss out on our opportunity for collaboration as other subregions will also express interest to be one of
the two "pilot" regions for this partnership.
I recognize that this is not the ideal time to be making important programmatic decisions given how many folks are out on
leave (I myself will be out on leave for 3 weeks after today), but we would request that Internews respond by the middle of
next week so that we can get back to Vera. As you will see in the draft concept note, this is a high-level initiative that
stems from a meeting between Administrator Power and YouTube CEO Susan Wojcicki.
If it would be helpful, I would be happy to jump on a call next week to discuss with the group if you have issues you want
to talk through. It would be great to include Josh Machleder in that conversation as well as he is helping coordinate this
initiative from the USAID/DRG side.
Thanks very much for your continuing engagement and collaboration on this important activity!
Best,
Nils.
Nils M. Mueller
Director, General Development Office
Regional Development Mission for Asia (RDMA)
US Agency for International Development (USAID)
[contact omitted]
On Wed, Jul 20, 2022 at 1:01 PM Rowan Reid < [opaque block] [contact omitted]> wrote:
HI Tina
Brian is on leave.
Based on what we co-designed with the USAID team there could be some synergies with Activity 2.3 and the Youtube
collaboration.
Activity 2.3: Disinformation Investigations
Building on the "pre-bunking" reports in Activity 2.1, Internews will support journalists and civil society researchers to jointly
investigate, map and document disinformation actors and networks and then communicate their findings. Specific focus will be
given to disinformation related to democracy, human rights, and governance (e.g., elections). Investigations will focus on deceptive
behavior, such as media manipulation and the use of fake online accounts. This could also include a deep dive into monetization of
disinformation as a tool for engagement with large platforms like Google and Facebook to drive accountability. Reporting will help
communicate such disinformation tactics to the public, and investigations will ultimately seek to gather enough evidence to

attribute disinformation campaigns to specific actors to hold them publicly accountable. Participants will learn how to identify and
document deceptive behavior associated with organized disinformation campaigns, enabling journalists to investigate the actors
behind disinformation campaigns, as well as addressing the content or narratives that is being circulated.
Outputs: 12 collaborative story grants (two grants for six countries), resulting in 12 stories
Next week will not work for us, but possibly the week after or we could save it for the start up meeting when we will all
be together in Bangkok September 12/13.
Rowan
From: Tinaflor Chaingam <[contact omitted]>
Sent: Tuesday,19 July 2022 6:21 PM
To: Brian Hanley s [opaque block] [contact omitted]>
Cc: Rowan Reid < [opaque block] [contact omitted]>; Amy Sim [opaque block] [contact omitted]>; Dan Spealman
[opaque block] [contact omitted]>; Rafiq Copeland - [opaque block] [contact omitted]>; Elizabeth Callender
<[contact omitted]>; Nils Mueller <[contact omitted]>; Leslie Maccracken <[contact omitted]>;
Christopher Adams <[contact omitted]>; Joshua Machleder <[contact omitted]>
Subject: Potential synergies with YouTube
Hi Brian,
Hope this email finds you well. Our colleagues in Washington recently shared the news that Youtube is seeking to
collaborate with USAID on supporting investigative journalism and influencers to counter information discorder through
small grants, capacity building and utilizing its platform to reach diverse groups of audiences. There are pros and cons
that we see from the end but we would like to seek your inputs and gauge your interest. Would this be something
viable to implement through the "Bolstering Media and Information Human Rights in Southeast Asia" (which we would
propose to change to "Media and Human Rights in SEA" moving forward for simplification)?
Please let me know what your schedule looks like next week/the following week. We could schedule a follow up call
and invite Johsua to provide more details as needed.
Best,
Tina
Tinaflor Chaingam
Project Management Specialist
General Development Office (GDO)
US Agency for International Development (USAID)/RDMA
Bangkok. Thailand
